understanding.purpose: 对比六个重点城市四个季度的GDP增速，并结合说明理解各城市的经济表现。
understanding.reading: 读者主要横向比较同一城市的季度变化，也会纵向比较不同城市在同一季度的增速；说明提供背景，通常在发现差异后阅读。说明文字较长，会主导各数据行的高度，因此城市名和增速可以利用同一行已有的高度保持清晰。
groups: 第2至第5列都是季度增速，作用相同，应保持相同宽度，便于横向和纵向比较。
第1列城市名标识整行；第6列说明为该城市的增速提供背景。
may_wrap: 说明中的中文叙述可自然换行。
空间紧张时，季度子表头可换行；四列应采用一致的宽度和换行节奏。
跨四列的总表头可在必要时换行。

bad.why: The quarter columns are much wider than their numbers need, leaving the notes in a narrow strip. Notes run to as many as nine lines, making rows excessively tall and separating the figures for successive cities.
It duplicates r1B: wide numeric columns squeeze the notes and produce the same excessive row heights.
Each quarter heading breaks into three single-character lines, making the headings slow to scan; the notes gain little compared with r2B.
The quarter headings break into three single-character lines, while the note wrapping and row heights remain essentially the same as r1C.

final.rationale: r2B keeps the four quarter columns equal, so their values are easy to compare, and gives the long notes enough width to read as prose. Its quarter headings wrap to two lines rather than three, preserving a clearer header hierarchy without imposing the very tall rows of r1B. The ranges are approximate and coupled: widening all four quarter columns requires narrowing the notes column to keep the total at or below 479px.

general: Columns with the same role benefit from consistent widths when readers compare their values.
Allocate width according to both content and reading task; unused space in short numeric cells can be more useful to prose.
Header wrapping should be judged alongside body wrapping and row rhythm.
specific: The quarter values are short, but their three-character headings create a sharp choice between two-line and three-line headers.
Long notes determine the height of every data row, so narrowing the notes column has a large effect on the whole table.

final.tradeoffs: r3A and r3C give the notes more room and shorten the table, but their quarter headings stack one character per line. r2A retains two-line headings but makes several notes longer than in r2B.
final.uncertain: A designer prioritizing note reading and a shorter table could reasonably prefer r3C; a designer prioritizing quick identification of the quarters may find its three-line headings too disruptive. The stated width ranges are estimates around the rendered preference, not separately tested layouts.

A.why: The description column is extremely narrow, breaking prose into fragments and making each row very tall. The quarter columns contain large stretches of unused space.

B.why: City names and quarter headers stay intact, making the figures easy to scan. The narrow description column produces long rows and frequent wrapping.

C.why: Equal quarter columns support comparison, city names stay intact, and descriptions have useful width. Each quarter header breaks across two lines.

D.why: The wide description column reads comfortably, but city names and quarter headers break into individual characters, weakening row identification and header scanning.

E.why: City names remain intact and descriptions have room to read, but each quarter header breaks into three single-character lines.

F.why: City names and numbers remain intact, the equal quarter columns are easy to compare, and descriptions have a reasonable measure. Quarter headers still break across two lines.

reviews.unsure: B preserves the quarter headers on one line, which may matter more to readers focused primarily on comparing growth rates; C and F give the descriptions substantially more room.

A.why: City names and figures stay intact, the four quarters have a consistent rhythm, and the notes have enough width to read comfortably. Each quarter header breaks across two lines.

B.why: The quarter columns are evenly sized and the city names and figures remain intact. The notes are slightly narrower than in A, creating more wrapping, while the quarter headers still break across two lines.

C.why: All quarter headers fit on one line, making the numerical group easy to scan. The narrow notes column creates many short lines and tall rows, leaving substantial empty space below the figures.

D.why: The notes are squeezed into extremely short lines, making them difficult to read and stretching each row far beyond its numerical content. The quarter columns are much wider than their figures need.

E.why: The notes have useful width, but every city name is split vertically and each quarter header runs over three lines. This weakens identification of rows and slows scanning of the quarter group.

F.why: City names and figures remain intact and the notes are relatively comfortable to read. However, each quarter header breaks into three single-character lines, making the comparison headings harder to scan.

reviews.unsure: The trade-off between A's two-line quarter headings and F's wider notes is somewhat subjective; A preserves a clearer quarter hierarchy while keeping the notes readable.
